subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is source-level trajectory/transcript filtering enough to close this issue, or should maintainers require a fresh current-main Windows provider proof for `openclaw chat --session <fresh-key>`?
rationale: The code now has the expected guardrails, but the reported failure is high-cost provider billing and has not been re-proven or disproven on current main.

options.title: Require current-main proof
options.body: Keep this open until a live or packaged current-main run shows large trajectory sidecars do not affect fresh-session prompts or provider input tokens.

options.title: Close from source guardrails
options.body: Accept the current trajectory/transcript/memory filters as sufficient and close without a new provider-billing proof.

options.title: Sponsor a targeted diagnostic
options.body: Have an owner add a narrow proof or diagnostic that logs prompt source byte categories before deciding close versus patch.

recommendation.title: Require current-main proof
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a live or packaged current-main run shows large trajectory sidecars do not affect fresh-session prompts or provider input tokens.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current evidence and recent history are in session artifact classification, cleanup, and docs touched by steipete.
